name: applyy
description: Job application automation: ATS discovery, resume tailoring with an honesty auditor, human-gated submission, and email-driven tracking.

scripts.test: pnpm run test:functions && pnpm run test:api && pnpm run test:workspace

// scripts: Every recursive script uses --if-present. Two of them were fatal without it: `build` broke every Vercel deploy, and `lint` would have broken the moment anything invoked it.
// scripts.test: Split 2026-09-10 because `pnpm -r run test` could NEVER reach supabase/functions: it is not a pnpm workspace member, has no package.json, and its files did not match any package's test/**/*.test.ts glob. That left 31 passing tests over the KILL SWITCH - the one row that halts every agent - unreachable by every runner in the repo. They passed when run by hand, which is what made it invisible: TEST QUALITY AND TEST REACHABILITY ARE INDEPENDENT PROPERTIES, and reading the tests only tells you about the first. Anyone opening that directory concluded the guard was covered.
// scripts.test:functions: Run directly by path rather than by making supabase/functions a workspace member. That tree is a DENO project with its own deno.json and deno.lock, and adding a package.json would put two dependency managers over one directory. deno.json also warns that Deno walking up the tree finds pnpm-workspace.yaml and rewrites this file - so the less this directory looks like an npm package, the better. Node runs them because deno.json excludes *.test.ts from deno check (they import node:test) and `deno test` accordingly finds no modules.
// scripts.test.ordering: Functions run FIRST, and the order is the whole point. The first version of this script ran the workspace first and `&&` meant that a pre-existing worker failure (3 tests in render-resume-pdf.test.ts) stopped the chain before the function tests reported - hiding the kill-switch results on the very first real invocation, which is precisely the visibility this script was written to create. `&&` masks whatever follows it exactly when something is already wrong, which is when you least want a safety-critical guard to go quiet. Functions are ~0.3s and cover the kill switch, so putting them first costs nothing and guarantees they always report. The remaining `&&` still gives CI one nonzero exit, and both halves stay individually invocable.
// scripts.test:api: Added 2026-11-01 with api/render-job-page.ts, for the same reachability reason as test:functions: api/ is not a workspace member, so no recursive script would ever find its tests. Run by path, second in `test` because it is fast (~0.3 s) and guards the SSRF rules of a function that runs a full browser on a server. NOTE: .github/workflows/ci.yml does not call `pnpm test`; it runs each node --test glob itself, so CI needs its own step for this glob too.
// scripts.build: WAS: `pnpm -r --filter "./packages/**" run build && pnpm -r --filter "./apps/**" run build`, which failed EVERY Vercel deploy with ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_NO_SCRIPT: neither packages/shared-types nor packages/resume-template has a build script. That absence is CORRECT and deliberate - both export raw .ts source with zero build step, which is what makes the Deno/Node/Vite cross-runtime guarantee work. So the script encoded an assumption the architecture deliberately rejects, the first half of the && chain failed, and apps/web was never reached. --if-present rather than deleting the packages half: a package that LATER gains a build step is then picked up automatically, whereas a hardcoded apps-only filter would silently stop building it. Derived over hardcoded - this project has been bitten three times by the hardcoded form.
// scripts.lint: Latent instance of the same bug, found while fixing build: NO package in the workspace defines a lint script, so this was guaranteed to fail the moment anything ran it. It had simply never been invoked.
// engines.node: Upper bound added 2026-09-10. Vercel warns that ">=24.0.0" auto-upgrades when a new Node major ships; an unbounded runtime range breaks a deploy months from now with no local change.
// dependencies: Root-level because the Vercel function api/render-job-page.ts lives at the repo root (vercel.json is here, so the Vercel project root is here) and Vercel installs and traces a root /api function against THIS package.json. Added 2026-11-01 when Teja moved the browser fallback for pasted job links into a Vercel function (Supabase Edge Functions cannot run a browser). playwright-core, not playwright: the client library only, no browser download; pinned to 1.55.1 to match the `playwright` pin in apps/web and worker. @sparticuz/chromium ships a Chromium build that runs on Vercel/Lambda; 140.0.0 because playwright-core 1.55.1 drives Chromium 140 (browsers.json: 140.0.7339.186), and a Chromium major newer than the client's protocol can break launch. Both EXACT, same reason as every pin in pnpm-workspace.yaml: a range that floats changes on a lockfile refresh nobody asked for. Production dependencies, not dev: the sparticuz README requires it when no Lambda layer is used, and Vercel must ship both in the function bundle.
